seo.description: Learn how to read a CDL MVR report step by step: license status, endorsements, violations and red flags for CDL-A drivers. Screen faster with Sentinel.
seo.keywords: CDL MVR report, how to read an MVR, motor vehicle record, CDL driver screening, ACD codes, serious violations, FMCSA MVR requirements

mainEntity.name: What does an MVR show for a CDL driver?

acceptedAnswer.text: It shows license status and class, endorsements and restrictions, moving violations and convictions, crashes where reported, and any suspensions or disqualifications on the commercial license.

mainEntity.name: How far back does a CDL MVR go?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most states report three to seven years of driving history, though serious commercial violations and disqualifications can appear for longer depending on the state.

mainEntity.name: Is an MVR the same as a PSP report?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. An MVR comes from the state DMV and covers license and violation history. A PSP report comes from FMCSA and covers roadside inspections and crashes. Complete screening uses both, and Sentinel pulls them together.

seo.title: What Is FMCSA Driver Safety Compliance? | Sentinel
seo.description: A plain-English guide to FMCSA driver safety compliance: DQ files, MVR reviews, PSP, Clearinghouse and CSA scores, and how to stay compliant with less work.
seo.keywords: FMCSA compliance, driver safety compliance, driver qualification file, 49 CFR 391.51, PSP report, Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse, CSA scores, annual MVR review

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between MVR and PSP in FMCSA compliance?

acceptedAnswer.text: The MVR is a state DMV record of license status and violations. The PSP is an FMCSA report of roadside inspections and crashes. A compliant screen uses both.

mainEntity.name: How often are MVR reviews required?

acceptedAnswer.text: At hire and at least once every 12 months for each driver, under 49 CFR 391.25.

mainEntity.name: Is the Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse mandatory?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A full pre-employment query is required before a driver performs safety-sensitive work, and a limited query is required at least annually.

mainEntity.name: What is the biggest red flag on a CDL driver record?

acceptedAnswer.text: A suspended, revoked or disqualified license is the most immediate red flag, followed by major violations such as DUI and a pattern of preventable crashes.

mainEntity.name: Can you hire a driver with violations on their MVR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, depending on the type, seriousness and age of the violation and your own safety standards. Serious violations and clear patterns are the ones to scrutinize.

mainEntity.name: What checks are required to hire a CDL-A driver?

acceptedAnswer.text: At minimum: license verification, an MVR, a Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse query, prior employment history for three years, and a valid DOT medical certificate. A PSP report is strongly recommended.

mainEntity.name: Do you need consent to run an MVR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires clear disclosure and written authorization before pulling a consumer report for employment.
